strings.name: Hou Yifan
strings.summary: Born in Xinghua, Hou joined the national team young, became a grandmaster at 14 and the youngest women’s world champion at 16. A four-time champion, she also competes in open events. She studied at Peking and Oxford, became a Shenzhen professor in 2020 and entered a Peking doctorate in chess neuroscience in 2026, connecting competition with education research.
strings.influence.rationale: Women’s world champion and high-level open tournament participant, advancing women chess players’ international influence.
strings.facts.f2.value: Peking bachelor’s (2016); Oxford MPP; began a Peking doctorate in 2026.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Four women’s world titles
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won the women’s world championship in 2010, 2011, 2013 and 2016.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Connecting chess and academia
strings.highlights.h2.text: Explores chess, education and cognition through university study and teaching.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Began Peking doctorate
strings.timeline.t1.text: Entered the psychology and cognitive sciences school to research chess neuroscience.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Shenzhen appointment
strings.timeline.t2.text: Became a Shenzhen University professor, bringing chess experience into university teaching.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Oxford studies
strings.timeline.t3.text: Entered Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar to study public policy.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Fourth world title
strings.timeline.t4.text: Beat Mariya Muzychuk to regain the women’s world title.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Third world title
strings.timeline.t5.text: Beat Anna Ushenina in a match to regain the world title.
strings.timeline.t6.title: World champion at 16
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won the women’s world championship, setting the youngest-winner record.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Grandmaster title
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned the open grandmaster title at 14.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Xinghua
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born in Xinghua, Jiangsu, beginning systematic chess training as a child.
